info.title: Ambivo Autonomous Agents API
info.description:
Autonomous AI agent endpoints for Ambivo CRM — Salesforce Agentforce-inspired architecture. ## Authentication All endpoints require a Bearer JWT token in the `Authorization` header. ## Response Pattern - **Success**: `{ "result": 1, ...data }` - **Error (Chat endpoints)**: `{ "result": 0, "error": "message" }` - **Error (Schema/Automation generators)**: `{ "result": 2, "error": "message" }` ## Architecture Overview The agent system has four tiers: ``` ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ /agent/chat (smart router entry point) │ │ ↓ │ │ AgentRouter (LLM-based intent classifier) │ │ ↓ confidence >= 0.7 ↓ fallback │ │ Direct Agent Chat SupervisorAgent │ │ (SmartLeadAgent, (multi-step │ │ RevenueAgent, etc.) orchestration) │ └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` **Available agents** (routable via `/agent/chat` or `/agent/chat/direct`). This list is `AGENT_CAPABILITIES` in `agents/agent_router.py`; `AgentRouter` itself only routes. | Agent | What it does | Example query | |---|---|---| | `RevenueAgent` | Revenue tracking and analysis | "What's my commission this month?" | | `SmartLeadAgent` | Lead management and qualification | "Show me stale leads from last 30 days" | | `SmartContactAgent` | Contact management and organization | "Find contacts at Microsoft" | | `SmartAccountAgent` | Account management and tracking | "Show account status for Apple Inc" | | `SmartOpportunityAgent` | Deal management and tracking | "Show deals in negotiation stage" | | `SmartOrderAgent` | Order processing and management | "Show pending orders" | | `AttributionAnalyticsAgent` | Marketing attribution analysis | "Which ad campaigns perform best?" | | `SmartBankAgent` | List connected bank institutions | "What banks am I connected to?" | | `SmartESignAgent` | List and search contract templates | "List all my templates" | | `DealCloseAgent` | Guided step-by-step deal closing | "I need to close a deal" | | `LeadQualityAgent` | Lead quality and disqualification analysis | "What's our lead quality this month?" | | `SmartCalendarAgent` | List connected calendars (Google, Microsoft) | "What's on my calendar today?" | | `SmartEmailAgent` | List connected email mailboxes | "Check my email" | | `SmartResearchAgent` | Research a person for sales outreach (name, title, pain points, outreach hooks) | "Research John Smith at Coca Cola" | | `SmartDataEnrichmentAgent` | Enrich a CRM record with structured firmographic/demographic fields from People Data Labs (lead, contact, or account) | "Enrich lead Flo" | | `SmartTaskAgent` | List tasks with rich filters: status, priority, assignee | "Show my tasks" | | `SmartWorkforceAgent` | Workforce: who is clocked in, on break, late or missing today; the roster and short-staffed shifts; hours, overtime and lateness; timecards to approve; shift swaps; covering and adding shifts | "Who is clocked in right now?" | | `SmartInventoryAgent` | Inventory: stock on hand by place, what is running low and what to reorder, out-of-stock and negative balances, movements and waste, expiring lots, stock value; recording issues, waste, adjustments and transfers | "How many 12oz cups do we have?" | | `SmartProcurementAgent` | Procurement: requisitions and purchase orders by stage, what awaits my approval, overdue and expected deliveries, spend by vendor, vendor prices; approving, ordering approved demand, receiving deliveries, closing orders | "What is waiting for my approval?" | | `SmartAssetBaseAgent` | AssetBase: find equipment by tag, serial or state; who has what and overdue loans; warranty and end-of-life alerts; book value; audits; expiring contracts; check out, check in, update condition, dispose, work orders, renewal purchase orders | "Which machines are out of service?" | | `SmartDailyPlanAgent` | Answer questions about today's synthesized productivity plan | "What should I work on today?" | | `EndpointAgent` | General-purpose API endpoint invocation | "Show me leads from Google source" | | `ProductHelpAgent` | Product how-to guidance from the Ambivo user guides | "How do I import my leads?" | Not routed by `/agent/chat`: `SalesPerformanceAgent` (`/user/tenant/agent_sales`), the data import agent (`/user/data_import/manage`), the daily plan generator (`/user/daily_plan/generate`), and the Schema and Automation generators below. > **Note on agent availability**: All agents are available via both `/agent/chat` (auto-routing) > and `/agent/chat/direct` (explicit targeting), including `SmartBankAgent` and `LeadQualityAgent`. **SSE streaming**: `/agent/chat` supports `"stream": true` for real-time token-by-token responses: ``` data: {"type": "token", "content": "chunk of text"} data: {"type": "metadata", "agent_used": "...", "data": [...]} data: {"type": "done"} ``` ## Agents as Workflow Nodes Multi-agent work is built as a **workflow in the AI Workflow System**, where each agent is a node (see the Workflows API). A document-reading flow, for example, is `ocr` → `llm` (extract to a JSON Schema) → `validate` → `condition` → a record node. Nothing in it is specific to one form: it is configuration. - `llm` and `validate` nodes are available. `document_extract`, `human_review` and a tool-using `ai_agent` node are planned. - Every AI call from a node goes through Core `POST /genai/complete` (CRM API), so the tenant's AI setting, quota and billing apply in one place. - A tenant can use its own AI provider keys, or its own inference endpoint, through the Ambivo LLM gateway (`Tenant.genai_via_gateway`). The chat agents on this page still use Ambivo's keys; moving them onto `/genai/complete` is planned. ## Business Flows (Multi-Step Orchestration) Predefined multi-agent workflows that chain steps together: - `lead_to_customer` — Full lead qualification pipeline - Execute via `/agent/flow/execute`, monitor via `/agent/flow/status` - Supports human-in-the-loop approvals via `/agent/approval/*` ## AI-Powered Generators All generators support **session_id conversation memory** — the agent collects requirements iteratively and returns `status: more-info-needed`, `qa-fixing`, or `complete`. Both Schema Generator and Automation Generator also support **edit mode** — pass an existing schema or rules on the first turn to modify them via natural language instead of starting from scratch. > **`tenant_scope` does NOT apply to generators.** The `tenant_scope` parameter only affects > chat endpoints (`/agent/chat` and `/agent/chat/direct`). Schema and automation generators > operate in the authenticated user's context and do not support tenant-wide scoping. ### Edit Mode — Evolving Existing Objects & Automations A common workflow is to start with a custom object or automation that was previously created (either via the UI or an earlier agent session), then use the agent to evolve it via natural language. This avoids re-describing the entire object from scratch and allows incremental refinement. **Use Case 1: Evolving an existing custom object schema** A user created a "To-Do" custom object via the UI with basic fields (name, status, due_date). Now they want to add a category dropdown, change status options, add an assignee reference, and remove the priority field. ``` Step 1: Fetch the existing schema from the tenant's custom objects GET /custom/objects → find the "todo" object → extract its schema_meta Step 2: POST /agent/schema/generate { "description": "Add a category dropdown with Work/Personal/Urgent, change status options to Open/In Progress/Done, add an assigned_to reference to users, and remove the priority field", "session_id": "AMB-1709712345-edit01", "include_full_metadata": true, "existing_schema": { "key": "todo", "label": "To-Do", "pluralLabel": "To-Dos", "description": "Track tasks and to-do items", "icon": "data_table", "color": "#989696", "primaryField": "name", "attributes": [ {"key": "name", "label": "Name", "type": "text", "required": true}, {"key": "status", "label": "Status", "type": "select", "config": { "options": [{"value": "todo", "label": "To Do"}, {"value": "done", "label": "Done"}] }}, {"key": "priority", "label": "Priority", "type": "select", "config": { "options": [{"value": "high", "label": "High"}, {"value": "low", "label": "Low"}] }}, {"key": "due_date", "label": "Due Date", "type": "date"} ] } } Step 3: Agent returns status: "complete" with the modified schema. - "name" and "due_date" preserved (untouched) - "status" options changed to Open/In Progress/Done - "priority" removed (user requested) - "category" added with Work/Personal/Urgent options - "assigned_to" added as user reference Use the returned schema_meta to update the object via PUT /custom/object/{id}. ``` **Use Case 2: Editing an existing automation rule** A user has an automation that sends an email when a lead is qualified. They want to change the recipient, add a 5-minute delay, and add a create_task action for follow-up. ``` Step 1: Fetch the existing automation rules GET /user/automations → find the relevant rule → extract its JSON Step 2: POST /agent/automation/generate { "description": "Change email recipient to sales@company.com, add 5 minute delay, and also create a follow-up task assigned to the lead owner", "session_id": "AMB-1709712345-edit02", "existing_rules": [ { "entity_type": "lead", "event_name": "update", "is_active": true, "is_custom_module_entity": false, "description": "Send email when lead qualified", "action_list": [ { "action_id": "a1b2c3d4-uuid", "action": "send_email", "level": "tenant", "data_level": "single", "initial_delay": 0, "match_criteria_dict": {}, "match_updated_fields_dict": {"lead_status": {"before": "*", "after": "qualified"}}, "args_payload": { "sender_name": "{{tenant_name}}", "sender_email": "noreply@ambivo.com", "message_subject": "Lead Qualified: {{name}}", "message_body": "

Lead {{name}} has been qualified.

", "to_list": ["admin@co.com"] } } ] } ] } Step 3: Agent returns status: "complete" with modified rules. - Original action_id "a1b2c3d4-uuid" preserved on the send_email action - Recipient changed from admin@co.com → sales@company.com - initial_delay changed from 0 → 300 (5 minutes in seconds) - New create_task action appended with new action_id - entity_type, event_name, match criteria all unchanged Use the returned automation_rules to update via PUT /user/automations/{id}. ``` **Use Case 3: Multi-turn edit with QA** ``` Turn 1: POST /agent/schema/generate { "description": "Add a category field", "session_id": "AMB-1709712345-edit03", "existing_schema": {"key":"todo","label":"To-Do","attributes":[{"key":"name","label":"Name","type":"text","required":true}]} } → status: "more-info-needed" → question: "What options should the category dropdown have?" Turn 2: POST /agent/schema/generate { "description": "Work, Personal, Urgent, Other", "session_id": "AMB-1709712345-edit03" ← same session_id, no existing_schema needed } → status: "complete" — modified schema with the new category field added alongside existing fields Turn 3 (optional): POST /agent/schema/generate { "description": "Actually make it a multiselect instead of select", "session_id": "AMB-1709712345-edit03" ← continues same session } → status: "complete" — category field type changed to multiselect, all other fields unchanged ``` **Key behaviors in edit mode:** - `existing_schema` / `existing_rules` are only sent on **Turn 1** — they persist in Redis session state - Existing fields/actions are **preserved** unless user explicitly asks to remove or change them - Agent returns the **complete** modified schema/rules (not a diff) - All QA validation (schema) and post-validation (automation) still applies - `session_id` must be reused across all turns in the conversation - Session state persists in Redis with 1-hour TTL - If the session expires (1-hour TTL), re-send `existing_schema` / `existing_rules` on the next request to start a new edit session ### Session Memory & Conversation State **Redis persistence**: All generators store conversation state in Redis: - Schema: key prefix `schema_conv_`, TTL 3600s - Automation: key prefix `automation_conv_`, TTL 3600s **Conversation history**: Each turn (user + assistant) is appended to the session's history array. The full history is included in LLM prompts for multi-turn context. This means follow-up turns can reference earlier parts of the conversation naturally. **Session expiry handling**: - Schema: If `session_id` provided but expired, returns error asking to start over - Automation: If `session_id` provided but expired, silently creates new session with `session_restarted: true` **Full description accumulation**: All user turns are concatenated with `" | "` separator and passed to the LLM as the complete description context. This prevents information loss across turns. | Generator | Endpoint | What It Does | |---|---|---| | Schema Generator | `/agent/schema/generate` | Natural language → custom object schema (create or edit via `existing_schema`) | | Schema App Designer | `/agent/schema/design-app` | Natural language → multi-object application design | | Schema Validator | `/agent/schema/validate` | QA validation for generated schemas | | Schema Refiner | `/agent/schema/refine` | Modify an existing schema via natural language | | Attribute Suggester | `/agent/schema/suggest-attributes` | AI-suggested fields for a given object type | | Schema Session Clear | `/agent/schema/clear` | Clear schema conversation session | | Automation Generator | `/agent/automation/generate` | Natural language → automation rules (create or edit via `existing_rules`) | | Automation Refiner | `/agent/automation/refine` | Modify an existing automation via natural language | | Automation Explainer | `/agent/automation/explain` | Explain an automation config in plain English | | Automation Session Clear | `/agent/automation/clear` | Clear automation conversation session | ## Attribution Analytics Dedicated endpoints for marketing attribution analysis: - Funnel metrics per source (`/agent/attribution/funnel`) - Cross-source comparison (`/agent/attribution/compare`) - ROI analysis with ad spend (`/agent/attribution/roi`) - Platform comparison (`/agent/attribution/platforms`) - Monthly trends (`/agent/attribution/trends`) - AI insights & recommendations (`/agent/attribution/insights`) - Natural language queries (`/agent/attribution/query`)

tags.name: Schema Generator
tags.description:
AI-powered custom object schema generation with iterative conversation and autonomous QA.

### Conversation Flow (session_id)

All schema generator endpoints support multi-turn conversations via `session_id`.
The frontend generates a session_id on page load and sends it with every request.
Conversation state is persisted in Redis (TTL: 1 hour).

```
Turn 1: POST /agent/schema/generate {description, session_id}
  → status: "more-info-needed" (agent needs clarification)
Turn 2: POST /agent/schema/generate {description: "user's answer", session_id}
  → status: "complete" OR "qa-fixing"
Turn 3 (if qa-fixing): POST /agent/schema/generate {description: "user's fix", session_id}
  → status: "complete"
```

### Edit Mode (existing_schema)

Pass `existing_schema` (JSON object or stringified JSON) on the **first turn** to edit an existing object
instead of creating from scratch. The agent modifies the supplied schema based on the description.
The existing schema is preserved in conversation state across all multi-turn interactions.

```
Turn 1: POST /agent/schema/generate {description: "add a priority field", existing_schema: {...}, session_id}
  → status: "complete" (modified schema returned)
```

### Response Statuses

| Status | Meaning | Next Action |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `more-info-needed` | Agent needs more details to generate | Send user's answer with same `session_id` |
| `qa-fixing` | Schema generated but QA found issues that need user input | Send user's guidance with same `session_id` |
| `complete` | Schema generated and QA passed | Use `schema_meta` / `full_metadata` to create object |

### QA Validation Loop

After generation, the QA agent autonomously validates the schema:
1. **Auto-fixable errors** (wrong types, missing config) → LLM fixes automatically (up to 2 retries)
2. **User-facing errors** (collection name collision, ambiguous references) → returns `qa-fixing` with questions
3. **QA passes** → returns `complete` with `qa_report` (score 0-100)
4. **Safety cap** (`MAX_TOTAL_QA_ITERATIONS = 6`) prevents infinite QA cycling — returns best schema with `qa_capped: true`

### Endpoints

| Endpoint | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `POST /agent/schema/generate` | Generate single object schema (iterative), or edit existing via `existing_schema` |
| `POST /agent/schema/design-app` | Design multi-object application with relationships (iterative) |
| `POST /agent/schema/validate` | Standalone QA validation |
| `POST /agent/schema/refine` | Refine an existing schema |
| `POST /agent/schema/suggest-attributes` | Suggest additional attributes |
| `POST /agent/schema/clear` | Clear conversation session |

tags.name: E-Sign
tags.description:
Natural language interface for e-signature operations via `SmartESignAgent`.

The agent wraps three underlying services:
- **ContractTemplateService** — template listing and retrieval
- **ContractInstanceService** — instance creation from templates, sending for signature
- **NativeESignService** — document status, signing links, cancellation, evidence packages

### Capabilities

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `list_templates` | List active contract templates (NDA, SOW, MSA, etc.) |
| `list_documents` | List e-sign documents with optional status filter |
| `get_document_status` | Detailed status with per-signer breakdown |
| `send_template` | Find template by name → create instance → send for signature |
| `get_signing_links` | Get per-signer signing URLs |
| `download_evidence` | Signed doc URL + audit trail info for completed documents |
| `cancel_document` | Cancel an active document |
| `resend_invitation` | Resend signing invitation to a specific signer |
| `verify_integrity` | SHA-256 hash verification |

### Status Mapping

Users use natural language terms; the agent maps them to system statuses:

| User says | System statuses queried |
|-----------|----------------------|
| "pending" / "awaiting" | `pending`, `sent`, `viewed`, `partially_signed` |
| "signed" / "completed" | `completed` |
| "cancelled" | `cancelled` |
| "declined" | `declined` |
| "expired" | `expired` |
| "draft" | `draft` |

### Multi-Step Send Flow

When a user says "Send the NDA to alex@acme.com", the agent:
1. Fuzzy-matches the template name from the tenant's active templates
2. Creates a `ContractInstance` with the signer(s)
3. Sends the instance for e-signature

If any step fails, a partial-success response explains what happened.

### Accessing via Chat

- **Auto-routed**: `POST /agent/chat` — the `AgentRouter` detects e-sign intent
- **Direct**: `POST /agent/chat/direct` with `agent_type: "SmartESignAgent"`

### Configuration

Tenant admins can customise the agent's system prompt via `ai_agent_config` with `agent_type: "esign"`.

tags.name: Calendar Agent
tags.description:
Natural language interface for calendar operations via `SmartCalendarAgent`.

The agent wraps calendar services for Google and Microsoft providers:
- **CalendarService** — calendar metadata, access control, timezone conversion
- **GoogleService** — Google Calendar API (events CRUD, sync)
- **MicrosoftService** — Microsoft Calendar API (events CRUD, sync)
- **UserMiscUtils** — schedule queries, event orchestration

### Capabilities

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `list_calendars` | List all connected calendars (Google, Microsoft) |
| `get_events` | View events in a date range with optional search |
| `get_free_slots` | Find available time slots with configurable duration |
| `create_event` | Create events with attendees, location, online meetings, recurrence |
| `update_event` | Update event details (time, attendees, location) |
| `delete_event` | Delete/cancel calendar events |
| `refresh_calendars` | Sync calendar list from Google/Microsoft providers |
| `set_default_calendar` | Set a specific calendar as default |

### Calendar Resolution

Users refer to calendars by name. The agent fuzzy-matches against calendar `summary` and `calendarID`:
1. Exact case-insensitive match
2. Substring containment
3. Word-level intersection

Falls back to default calendar if no name specified.

### Provider Auto-Detection

The agent reads the `provider` field from the calendar object and dispatches to
`GoogleService` or `MicrosoftService` transparently. Online meetings auto-generate
Google Meet or Microsoft Teams links.

### Accessing via Chat

- **Auto-routed**: `POST /agent/chat` — the `AgentRouter` detects calendar/scheduling intent
- **Direct**: `POST /agent/chat/direct` with `agent_type: "SmartCalendarAgent"`

### Configuration

Tenant admins can customise the agent's system prompt via `ai_agent_config` with `agent_type: "calendar"`.

tags.name: Email Agent
tags.description:
Natural language interface for email/mailbox operations via `SmartEmailAgent`.

The agent proxies operations through the email microservice for OAuth-connected mailboxes,
matching the same request/response patterns as the `/email/*` REST endpoints.

### Capabilities

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `list_mailboxes` | List connected OAuth email mailboxes |
| `list_folders` | Browse email folder tree |
| `search_emails` | Search by sender, subject, date, read status (IMAP syntax) |
| `read_email` | Read full email message by UID |
| `send_email` | Compose and send new emails |
| `reply_email` | Reply to an email (auto-populates threading headers) |
| `forward_email` | Forward an email to new recipients |
| `move_emails` | Move emails between folders |
| `mark_read_unread` | Mark emails as read or unread |
| `delete_emails` | Delete emails |
| `create_folder` | Create new email folders |

### Search Criteria

The agent translates natural language into IMAP SEARCH syntax:

| User says | IMAP criteria |
|-----------|---------------|
| "unread emails" | `UNSEEN` |
| "emails from john" | `FROM "john"` |
| "about the proposal" | `SUBJECT "proposal"` |
| "since Monday" | `SINCE "23-Mar-2026"` |

A search criteria sanitizer validates LLM output against an allowed IMAP keyword whitelist.

### Mailbox Resolution

- Single mailbox → auto-selected
- Multiple mailboxes → user specifies or agent asks
- All queries scoped to `userid` + `tenant_id` (no cross-user access)

### Accessing via Chat

- **Auto-routed**: `POST /agent/chat` — the `AgentRouter` detects email/inbox intent
- **Direct**: `POST /agent/chat/direct` with `agent_type: "SmartEmailAgent"`

### Configuration

Tenant admins can customise the agent's system prompt via `ai_agent_config` with `agent_type: "email"`.

tags.name: Automation Generator
tags.description:
**Deprecated.** Automation rules are replaced by workflows. `generate` and `refine`
return `{"result": 2, "error_code": "AUTOMATION_RULES_DEPRECATED"}` with a message
pointing to Workflows. Rules that already exist still run until they are moved.

AI-powered automation rule generation from natural language with iterative conversation.

### Conversation Flow (session_id)

Same multi-turn pattern as Schema Generator. The frontend generates a `session_id`
on page load and sends it with every request.

```
Turn 1: POST /agent/automation/generate {description, session_id}
  → status: "more-info-needed" (agent needs: who to email? what conditions?)
Turn 2: POST /agent/automation/generate {description: "send to admin@co.com when status is qualified", session_id}
  → status: "complete" with automation_rules[]
```

### Edit Mode (existing_rules)

Pass `existing_rules` (JSON array or stringified JSON) on the **first turn** to edit existing
automation rules instead of creating from scratch. The agent modifies the supplied rules based
on the description. Existing rules are preserved in conversation state across all turns.

```
Turn 1: POST /agent/automation/generate {description: "change recipient to sales@co.com", existing_rules: [...], session_id}
  → status: "complete" (modified rules returned)
```

### Response Statuses

| Status | Meaning | Next Action |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `more-info-needed` | Agent needs more details (recipient, conditions, etc.) | Send user's answer with same `session_id` |
| `complete` | Automation rules generated successfully | Use `automation_rules` to create via automation API |

### Validation

After generation, `_post_validate_rules()` checks for missing required args, event/cron coherence, and template variable format.
If errors are found, one auto-fix attempt is made via LLM. Rules are always returned — never blocked — with an optional `validation_report`.

### Session Recovery

If a `session_id` is provided but the Redis key has expired, the agent silently creates a new session and includes `session_restarted: true` in the response.

### Collected Fields

The `collected` dict accumulates resolved information across turns:
```json
{
  "entity_type": "lead",
  "event_name": "update",
  "action_type": "send_email",
  "action_fields": {"to_list": ["admin@co.com"]},
  "conditions": "status -> qualified",
  "delay": null
}
```

### Endpoints

| Endpoint | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `POST /agent/automation/generate` | Generate automation rules (iterative), or edit existing via `existing_rules` |
| `POST /agent/automation/refine` | Refine existing automation rules |
| `POST /agent/automation/explain` | Explain an automation rule in plain English |
| `POST /agent/automation/clear` | Clear conversation session |

tags.name: Agent Configuration
tags.description:
Per-tenant AI agent configuration management. Tenant admins can customize
agent behavior by overriding the system prompt, persona, settings, and actions
for each agent type.

### Key Concepts

- **Agent Type**: Each agent (deal_close, smart_lead, etc.) has a unique type string.
  A tenant can have **at most one config per agent type** — the upsert endpoint enforces this.
- **Seed Defaults**: Agents ship with built-in prompts. Custom configs override these.
  Deleting a config resets the agent to its seed default — there is no "blank" state.
- **Status**: Configs can be `active`, `inactive`, or `draft`.
  Only `active` configs are loaded by agents at runtime. Setting status to `inactive`
  effectively resets the agent to its seed default without deleting the config.

### Available Agent Types

| Type | Agent | Description |
|------|-------|-------------|
| `deal_close` | DealCloseAgent | Guided step-by-step deal closing with invoice calculation |
| `smart_lead` | SmartLeadAgent | Lead analytics and management |
| `smart_contact` | SmartContactAgent | Contact analytics and management |
| `smart_opportunity` | SmartOpportunityAgent | Pipeline analytics and management |
| `smart_account` | SmartAccountAgent | Account analytics and management |
| `smart_order` | SmartOrderAgent | Order analytics and management |
| `smart_attribution` | SmartAttributionAgent | Marketing attribution analytics |
| `revenue` | RevenueAgent | Revenue and commission tracking |
| `smart_bank` | SmartBankAgent | Banking and financial data |
| `esign` | SmartESignAgent | E-signature workflows and contract templates |
| `calendar` | SmartCalendarAgent | Calendar, events, and scheduling |
| `email` | SmartEmailAgent | Email, mailbox, and messaging |
| `schema_generator` | SchemaGeneratorAgent | AI-powered custom object schema generation |
| `automation_generator` | AutomationGeneratorAgent | AI-powered automation rule generation |

### Permissions

- **Read** (GET): Any authenticated user with an approved tenant account
- **Write** (POST, DELETE): Tenant admin only (`is_tenant_admin: true`)

### Typical UI Flow

```
1. GET /user/ai_agent_config/types         → populate agent type selector
2. GET /user/ai_agent_config/type/{type}    → load existing config or show "using defaults"
3. POST /user/ai_agent_config               → save changes (upserts by agent_type)
4. DELETE /user/ai_agent_config/type/{type}  → reset to defaults (confirmation dialog)
```

### Pagination

The list endpoint (`GET /user/ai_agent_config/list`) supports page-based pagination
with `page` and `limit` query parameters. Response includes `total`, `pages`, and
current `page` for building pagination controls.

post.description:
Main entry point for agent interactions. Automatically routes the message to
the best agent using `AgentRouter` (LLM-based intent classification).

**Routing logic**:
1. `AgentRouter.route_query()` scores the message against all agents
2. If confidence >= 0.7 → routes directly to the recommended agent's `.chat()` method
3. If confidence < 0.7 → falls back to `SupervisorAgent` for complex orchestration

**Streaming**: Set `"stream": true` for SSE (Server-Sent Events) output.
The response streams token-by-token with a final metadata event.

**`tenant_scope`**: When `true` (and user is tenant admin), queries return
all tenant records instead of only the current user's records. This parameter
is only effective on chat endpoints — it does NOT apply to schema or automation generators.
Enforced server-side: `tenant_scope = bool(args.get('tenant_scope', False)) and self.is_tenant_admin`.

**Entity pinning via `context`** — when the frontend passes
`entity_type: <type>` and `entity_id: <24-hex>` inside the `context`
string, the endpoint appends a `[[CTX_ENTITY:type=…,id=…]]`
sentinel and remembers both values. This unlocks two behaviors:
  1. Router override — if the router picks a *different* CRM entity
     agent than the pinned type (e.g. SmartContactAgent when the
     user is on a lead), it is re-routed to the pinned entity's
     agent.
  2. Draft-composition fast-path — when the message matches a
     draft intent ("craft/draft/compose/write" + "email/sms/text/
     follow-up/…") AND an `entity_id` is resolved, the pinned
     entity's smart agent runs the `compose_message_draft` action
     instead of routing to SmartEmailAgent. Returns grounded
     drafts with a `drafts` / `ground_truth_used` /
     `hallucination_flags` payload (see the `compose_draft` example
     under responses).

post.summary: Generate custom object schema from natural language
post.description:
AI-powered schema generation with iterative conversation and autonomous QA validation.
Supports both **create mode** (new object) and **edit mode** (modify existing object via `existing_schema`).

**Conversation flow:**
1. Send a description with a `session_id` (and optionally `existing_schema` to edit)
2. If the agent needs clarification → `status: "more-info-needed"` with `questions`
3. Re-send with user's answer and same `session_id`
4. When enough info → agent generates schema → QA validates
5. If QA auto-fixes succeed → `status: "complete"` with `qa_report`
6. If QA finds user-facing issues → `status: "qa-fixing"` with `questions`
7. Re-send with user's guidance and same `session_id` → QA re-validates

**Edit mode:** When `existing_schema` is provided, the agent modifies the supplied schema
based on the description rather than creating from scratch. Existing fields are preserved
unless the user explicitly asks to remove or change them. The existing schema is persisted
in conversation state across all multi-turn interactions — only send it on the first turn.

**Example descriptions**:
- "I need a to-do application to track my task list"
- "Property management app to track rental properties with tenants and payments"
- "Add a priority dropdown and remove the notes field" _(edit mode)_

session_id.description:
Session ID for conversation continuity. Frontend generates on page load
(e.g. `AMB-<timestamp>-<random>`). Auto-generated if omitted.
**Must be reused across turns** to maintain conversation memory.

NOT need to send this. If provided, it is ignored in favor of the server-side fetch.

existing_schema.description:
Existing schema to edit instead of creating from scratch. Accepts either a JSON object
or a stringified JSON string. When provided, the agent operates in **edit mode** —
it modifies the supplied schema based on the `description`. The existing schema is
persisted in conversation state across all turns; only send it on the **first turn**.
Subsequent turns use `session_id` to continue the conversation.

parameters.description: MongoDB ObjectId of the config document

example.msg: Agent config for 'deal_close' deleted. Agent will use seed defaults.

post.description:
Authenticates a user with email and password credentials. Returns user
profile information along with access and refresh JWT tokens.

The client should include device metadata for session tracking.

Exchanges a valid refresh token for a new access token. Called
automatically by the client when a request returns HTTP 401.

401.description: Refresh token is invalid or expired

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of folders and files for the authenticated user.
Supports sorting, pagination, and MongoDB-style match filters.

parameters.name: folders_first
parameters.description: When true, folders are listed before files.

pdf_url.description: Presigned S3 URL for the template PDF (7-year expiry, auto-refreshed)

order.description: Signing order (1-based). Enforced for sequential multi-party signing.

pdf_url.description: Signed PDF URL if completed, otherwise original PDF URL

response.description: Natural language response from the agent

query_type.description: Type of query executed (list, aggregate, count, etc.)

pending_approvals.description: Approvals waiting for human decision (fallback path)

fallback_to_supervisor.description: Whether the query fell back to SupervisorAgent

status.description: Overall status of the agent response

recommended_agent.description: Agent recommended by the supervisor (fallback path)

questions.description: Clarifying questions when status is more-info-needed

qa_report.description: Quality assurance report for the response

query_executed.description: Details of the executed query (MongoDB pipeline, filters, etc.)

entity_type.description: Canonical entity type the agent acted on (lead, contact, account, opportunity, task, email, etc.)

entity_id.description: 24-char hex ObjectId of the entity the action targeted (populated by `compose_message_draft` and other per-entity actions)

intent.description:
Parsed draft intent — returned when the pinned-entity draft
fast-path fires (see `compose_message_draft` behaviour under
`/agent/chat`).

tone.description: Draft tone used by the LLM.

recipient_email.description: Primary email resolved from the pinned entity record (may be absent or an `@invalid.ambivo.com` placeholder when the record has no valid address).

drafts.description:
Grounded drafts produced by `compose_message_draft`. Each
channel is OPTIONAL — absent when not requested or when the
LLM failed to produce a valid result for that channel.
Drafts are NOT sent by this endpoint; the UI previews them
and calls the existing email/SMS send endpoints if the user
approves.

body.description: Plain text, capped at 4000 chars server-side. No signature block (the sending system appends signatures).

ground_truth_used.description:
The strict whitelist of facts the LLM was allowed to cite.
Anything NOT in this object was forbidden by the prompt.
Free-text fields (business_need, comments, employer, title)
are run through a prompt-injection neutralizer before being
shown to the LLM, so attacker-controlled markers like
"[[", "```", or "SYSTEM:" are stripped.

last_touchpoint.description: YYYY-MM-DD or empty string; derived from `last_touchpoint_ts` / `last_contacted_ts` / `updated_ts`.

recent_comments.description: Up to 5 most recent `type:user_comment` entries, each prefixed with [YYYY-MM-DD].

hallucination_flags.description:
Post-hoc heuristic flags on the LLM output. Each flag is
advisory (does NOT block the draft) and has the form
`<channel>:<category>:<snippet>`. Categories:
  - `unvetted_url` — URL in the draft that was not present in any ground-truth field
  - `unvetted_money` — dollar figure not in the ground truth
  - `unvetted_time_reference` — time phrase ("this week", "tomorrow", "next month", weekday names) not present verbatim in the ground truth
The UI should surface flags to the reviewer before the send
step.

AgentDirectResponse.description: Full standardized NL Query response from a specific agent

device_id.description: Persistent unique identifier for the client device

module_access.description: Map of module names to access levels

refresh_token.description: The refresh token obtained from login

AgentConfigResponse.description:
Full agent configuration object. Returned by all GET and POST endpoints.
The `id` field is a convenience alias for `ai_agent_config_id`.

system_prompt.description: The full system prompt that drives agent behavior

persona.description: Short persona description used alongside the system prompt

AgentTypeInfo.description: Metadata about a registered agent type (from `/user/ai_agent_config/types`).

has_seed_prompt.description:
Whether this agent ships with a built-in default prompt.
Agents without seed prompts require a custom config to function.

UpsertAgentConfigRequest.description:
Request body for creating or updating an agent config. Only `agent_type` is required.
On update, only provided fields are changed — omitted fields are left untouched.
On create, omitted fields use defaults (empty string, empty list, etc.).

agent_type.description:
Agent type identifier. Must be one of the registered types
(see `GET /user/ai_agent_config/types`).

system_prompt.description:
The full system prompt that drives agent behavior. This is the primary
customization field — it controls field terminology, question ordering,
validation rules, and conversational tone.

persona.description: Short persona description used alongside the system prompt

settings_dict.description:
Agent-specific settings as a JSON object. Structure varies by agent type.
Example for deal_close: `{"commission_rates": [25, 50, 100], "require_confirmation": true}`

keywords.description: Routing keywords for intent matching (e.g. `["close deal", "submit deal"]`)

status.description:
Config status. Only `active` configs are loaded by agents at runtime.
Set to `inactive` to temporarily disable without deleting.
Default on create: `active`.
